newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador president's old rival to sue for slander.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador president's old rival to sue for slander.

text.p: Former Ecuadoran presidential candidate Jaime Nebot, the Christian Democrat who lost to Abdala Bucaram last July, said in an interview published Tuesday he plans to sue President Bucaram for slander.

Rightist leader Nebot, who trailed the populist Bucaram in last year's election by about nine points, told the Expreso newspaper he will file a suit against the president Thursday, when Bucaram returns from an official visit to Peru.

Before setting off on his tour of Nicaragua, Panama and neighboring Peru, Bucaram accused Nebot of embezzling $5.0 million from a road construction project in the port city of Guayaquil -- Bucaram's power base, where he was once mayor.
"He will answer to the courts for that insult," said Nebot, who like Bucaram is a lawyer of Lebanese descent.
Nebot wondered aloud how Bucaram came by his wealth. Allegations of corruption that once got to court sent Bucaram into self-imposed exile while he was still mayor of Guayaquil.
Bucaram portrays himself as champion of Ecuador's poor and dispossessed, but has his home in one of Guayaquil's richest suburbs and bristles when journalists ask about his wealth.
"If he didn't win the lottery or inherit money or work, how come he is so rich now?" asked Nebot.
